text:
No, we can't certify that no fire occurred. We can only say that no thermal detection was recorded.

**What the evidence supports:** NASA FIRMS recorded zero thermal anomaly detections intersecting ASSET-F06 between 2026-10-06 and 2026-11-05. All four sensors (VIIRS S-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21 and MODIS) covered every day of that period, so the absence of detections isn't a data gap.

**What it doesn't establish:**
- That no fire occurred. Small, short-lived, cool or cloud-obscured fires can go undetected, especially at 375 m (VIIRS) and 1 km (MODIS) resolution.
- Whether there is any burned area.
- The cause of any change on the ground.
- Anything outside the evaluated period.

**Suggested wording:** "No FIRMS thermal detections intersected the asset during 6 Oct–5 Nov 2026, with full sensor coverage." If you need stronger assurance, you'd need complementary evidence such as burned-area mapping or optical imagery review.
